title: QuantumTrade19
explain: A lightweight desktop app that watches CoinDCX futures prices, finds key price levels (POIs), spots the 123Bull and 123Bear candle setups around them, scores them, alerts you, and later places trades by hand and then automatically.

title: Phase 3 - Automatic trading (Files 13-14)

title: Setup outcome tracker (read-only)
explain: Entry = Candle 3 close. SL = lowest (Bull) or highest (Bear) OHLC of Candle 1 to 3, minus or plus the buffer. Risk in ticks. SL Hit = wick touch before 1.5R. 1.5R reached = win; the trade closes when price returns to the 1.5R price and records the peak RRR. Not hit and not closed = Open. Stores the first touch time of each RRR level (steps of 0.5R), the SL time and the deepest adverse dip.

title: Risk amount and quantity

title: Lot-size worker with per-symbol leverage
explain: Quantity = risk amount divided by stop distance, respecting leverage and tick size.

title: Sizing and TP selector: Fixed Risk, or Fixed RRR with a fixed margin
explain: Decision D: one selector. Fixed Risk sizes the trade from your flat risk amount and the SL distance, TP by RRR. Fixed RRR uses a fixed margin amount, TP by RRR.

title: Net RRR: take profit set so the ratio holds after fees
explain: Decision D: the TP distance includes the round-trip fee, so the reward-to-risk ratio you chose is the ratio you actually get.

title: Leverage 1 to 5000 with broker cap, experiment switch and liquidation check
explain: Decision F: default cap = the symbol's broker maximum. The experiment switch allows up to 5000 and tags the trade. A trade is rejected when liquidation would come before the stop loss.

title: Five trailing methods plus the automatic selector
explain: ATR, structure, fixed-step, chandelier and breakeven-then-ATR, all in the first version. The stop only moves in the favourable direction; breakeven includes fees. Manual override per trade.

title: Gate: hand-worked examples match exactly (fees, SL, both sizing modes, net RRR, liquidation, 5 trailing methods)
explain: The acceptance test for FT-2. You confirm before lock.

title: Step 1 - FT-3 Alert system: Discord + Telegram (File 06)
explain: Built first (Jay, 24-10-2026). Every important moment becomes a premium, human-sounding message on Discord and Telegram, with Info / Important / Critical levels. Texts, icons and layout are planned with Jay before the code. Trade numbers (entry, SL, TP, quantity) join the messages after Step 2. OS popups stay deferred.

title: Message template
explain: One readable shape for every alert.

title: Discord notifier: several webhooks, on/off switch
explain: Sends the same message to every enabled channel.

title: Pacing queue so bursts never hit rate limits
explain: Prevents Discord 429 errors during busy moments.

title: Alerts tab list, newest first
explain: Every fired alert is listed in the Alerts tab.

title: Telegram notifier: several chats, on/off switch
explain: Sends the same message to every enabled chat, with its own pacing.

title: Alert levels: Info, Important, Critical, with routing per level
explain: Decision E: each level goes to chosen channels. Critical alerts (liquidation, feed down) ignore snooze.

title: Situation catalogue and message style guide, approved by Jay before code
explain: All situations (market watch, setup lifecycle, trade lifecycle, account and risk, system health, daily summary) with the text, icon and layout of each. Jay approves the samples first.

title: Webhooks and bot token in secure storage; Send-test-alert button
explain: Secrets never go into data/settings.json (it is pushed to GitHub). The test button posts every template to a private test channel.

title: Quiet hours, duplicate guard, per-symbol rate limit, snooze
explain: Keeps alerts calm and useful. The same alert is never sent twice.

title: Trade-plan fields (entry, SL, TP, quantity) added to messages after Step 2
explain: Wired once the Risk math exists, so 'setup confirmed' shows the real numbers.

title: Gate: Discord and Telegram, 2+ recipients each, 20-alert burst, level routing, no drops or duplicates
explain: The acceptance test for FT-3. Includes a snooze test: Critical alerts still arrive.

title: Step 3 - FT-4 Paper broker account
explain: A virtual account that behaves like a broker. Flat starting balance and flat risk amount are set in the Trading Panel. Works for any symbol; each symbol's tick size, fees and maximum leverage are loaded automatically.

title: Virtual account: balance, equity, margin, free margin
explain: The basic account numbers.

title: Broker factors with defaults
explain: Leverage 1 to 5000 (default cap = the symbol's broker maximum; an experiment switch allows more and tags those trades as not broker-realistic), maker/taker fee plus GST, slippage (version 1: fixed ticks plus taker fee, replaceable model), minimum lot, tick size, liquidation level, funding and spread. All editable.

title: Ledger: positions, fills, realized and unrealized PnL
explain: Never touches the real broker.

title: Settings card with editable defaults and reset
explain: Matches the locked UI style.

title: Gate: fabricated-price round trip matches a hand calculation
explain: The acceptance test for FT-4.

title: Step 5 - FT-5 Paper journal and profit/loss report (File 07, reduced)
explain: Trade, day, X-day, week, X-week, month and X-month overviews with KPI cards. Gives the true paper profit and loss of the strategy without the Confidence Score: the baseline for Step 6.

title: Trade logger (paper/live tag, auto/manual source)
explain: Every trade with entry, SL, TP, quantity, exit reason and net PnL.

title: Aggregator for all the period views
explain: Updates incrementally as trades are added.

title: KPI cards and equity curve
explain: Win rate, net PnL, profit factor, average R, drawdown, best and worst.

title: Setup snapshot saved with every paper trade
explain: Lets the Confidence Score be calculated later on the old trades, so Step 6 can be compared with the baseline.

title: Realism check: modelled fees against a real CoinDCX statement
explain: Jay compares the modelled fee and PnL with a real small trade statement. QT19 places no order.

title: Gate: 20 simulated trades; totals equal the sum of the trades
explain: The acceptance test for FT-5.

title: Step 4 - FT-6 Paper execution, trailing and auto paper trades (Files 11-14, paper only)
explain: The 'hands' in paper mode: fills with slippage, position tracking, all five trailing methods, the opposite-setup exit, and automatic paper trades from confirmed 4H High/Low and PDH/PDL setups. The confidence gate is a pass-through until Step 6. No real order can be placed.

title: Mode router: Paper / Live toggle
explain: Routes each order to the paper simulator or the real broker.

title: Paper simulator on FT-4, order placement, fill and slippage guard
explain: A fill that slips too far is rejected and logged.

title: Position manager, TP methods, trailing SL, opposite-setup exit
explain: The single source of truth for open positions.

title: Auto paper trades from confirmed setups (4H High/Low, PDH/PDL; 1m, 5m, 15m)
explain: The confidence gate is a pass-through until Step 6. Trade Allowed switch per symbol still applies.

title: Realistic exits: stop loss as market order, take profit as limit order
explain: SL = slippage plus taker fee. TP fills only when price trades through the level (maker fee). If both are touched in one candle, the stop loss counts first.

title: Gate: 20 manual and 20 auto paper trades; SL, TP and PnL match FT-2 by hand
explain: The acceptance test for FT-6. You confirm before lock.

title: Step 7 - FT-7 Auto trade with a Paper/Live switch (Files 13-14)
explain: The software trades by itself when the score passes. Real money is switched on only after a soak test and only by Jay's own action.

title: Manual/Auto switch per symbol (default Manual)
explain: A symbol trades itself only after you flip it to Auto.

title: Circuit breaker, max-concurrent guard, Dry-Run (default ON)
explain: Safety nets: auto falls back to alerts when a data engine is unhealthy; Dry-Run sends even 'Live' orders to paper.

title: Soak test in Paper/Dry-Run (blueprint: 1 week, 3+ symbols)
explain: The only waiting period in the plan; it protects real money.

title: Live switch: smallest risk first, then scale
explain: At least one more week at the smallest risk setting before full size.

title: Decision A: stop-loss source = both, with a switch; default = setup candles
explain: Decided by Jay on 22-10-2026: the quantity calculator supports both the SL found from the setup candles and an SL price typed per symbol, with a switch. Default is the setup candles.

title: Decision B: fast-track plan goes first
explain: Decided by Jay on 22-10-2026: the fast-track plan FT-0 to FT-7 is built before the older roadmap tracks (File 04 re-validation, Track 2, Track 3, File 04.1b, File 04.3, Track 6). Tracker A4 order is superseded once the TRACKER update is recorded.

title: Decision C: paper trading and alerts come before the Confidence Score
explain: Decided by Jay on 24-10-2026. Order: alerts, risk math, paper account, paper execution with trailing and auto paper trades, paper journal, Confidence Score, then live auto trade. Works for any symbol.

title: Decision D: one sizing and TP selector; RRR is net of fees
explain: Decided by Jay on 24-10-2026: Fixed Risk (size from risk, TP by RRR) or Fixed RRR with a fixed margin. Flat balance and flat risk amount are set in the Trading Panel.

title: Decision E: alert levels Info, Important, Critical with routing
explain: Decided by Jay on 24-10-2026: alerts for Discord and Telegram are built first, with levels and routing.

title: Decision F: leverage 1 to 5000 with broker cap; all five trailing methods; slippage v1
explain: Decided by Jay on 24-10-2026: default leverage cap = the symbol's broker maximum, plus an experiment switch. All five trailing methods in the first version. Slippage version 1 = fixed ticks plus taker fee, other models later.

title: Decision G: Confidence Score rules
explain: Decided by Jay on 24-10-2026: all 20 filters default ON; partial points allowed (the AI proposes the steps, Jay approves); any timeframe; scored at the setup's own confirmation; a filter that cannot be scored is left out and the rest rescaled.

title: Open: MTF filters 10-11 rule, journal filters 15-17 without history, filters 13-14 without data
explain: Waits for Step 6. Proposal: compare with the latest same-direction setup on 15m/5m (opposite = 0, none = left out); journal filters left out until history exists; 13 and 14 used only when their data exists.

title: Decision I: Independent POI design replaces File 04.1b Part A
explain: Decided by Jay on 24-10-2026: right-click add and delete, numbered Ind. POI labels, draggable, style in the right-click menu, cap of 10 per symbol, one line for 1m, 5m and 15m, saved across restarts, paper-only by default with a per-line live switch. Chart tools and the bug fix come before Step 1.
